text: The deposition frame is doing real work here -- every time Renata insists she's being professional, the gap between what the form permits and what she experienced widens into something genuinely unsettling. The debt ledger section is devastating in its flatness. Names, numbers, the phrase 'debts are heritable' sitting there without commentary, and you feel the weight of it more than if the narrator had editorialized for pages. I also appreciated that the supernatural elements remain honestly ambiguous. The corrupted photographs, the corridor that shortens -- these could be a woman losing her mind in an empty house. The story doesn't choose, and it's stronger for it. My one reservation is that the hand-in-the-wall climax feels slightly overstated after so much careful restraint. But the final line about the deposition not resuming is perfect -- the bureaucratic silence says more than any resolution could.
